scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what's going on here. There's this guy, let's call him G, who's been my best friend since kindergarten. My twin sister and G have always been really close, almost like they had a "thing" going on, but they never officially dated for a long time. Then, when we were all 17, they finally started dating, and everything was great for about 13 months. But then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and told my sister, even though G begged me not to. I was mad at him, and he was mad at me, so we didn't talk for a month and a half. That was really weird and hard for me because G is like my brother, and not having him around felt unbearable. After that, G invited me on his family ski trip to make things right, and I went. I ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry, and he even cried because he felt so bad. G and my sister broke up right after she found out, and they're still not speaking. My sister is really upset with me for still being friends with G, and she doesn't understand why I'm not ending our 13-year friendship over this. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it, but I don't want to lose our friendship. I think about it like this: if my best friend cheated on their significant other and felt bad about it, would I end our friendship? Probably not. So why should it be any different just because his significant other happened to be my sister? We're also planning to go to the same college in the fall, which is in a different state from where my sister is going. So, none of this will be something we think about much when we're living apart. Am I the asshole for not ending my friendship with G after he cheated on my sister? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, what defines a friendship? Is it about loyalty, understanding, or forgiveness? Then, how does cheating affect these dynamics, especially when it involves someone close to you like your sister? Also, how does the relationship between G and my sister factor into this? They're not speaking anymore, which adds another layer of complexity. I also need to think about the impact on my sister. She's hurt, and she's probably feeling betrayed not just by G but also by me for not taking her side. On the other hand, G has shown genuine remorse, and our friendship has a long history. It's not easy to walk away from that, especially when you've been through so much together. Another angle is to consider how this situation might affect our future. If we stay friends, will there be lingering resentment? Or can we move past it and maintain a healthy relationship? Also, how does this decision affect my relationship with my sister? Will it strain our bond, or can we find a way to understand each other's perspectives? I also wonder about the broader implications of forgiveness. Is it always the right choice, or are there times when walking away is healthier for everyone involved? In this case, since G has apologized and shown regret, does that make it easier to forgive him? Or does the fact that he cheated on my sister, someone I care deeply about, make it harder to overlook? Additionally, I should think about the advice I would give to someone else in a similar situation. If a friend cheated on my sibling, would I advise them to end the friendship, or would I encourage them to work through it? This could help me see the situation more objectively. Lastly, I need to reflect on my own feelings and boundaries. How do I feel about continuing the friendship with G? Am I holding onto it because it's convenient, or because I genuinely value the relationship? Am I willing to accept the potential consequences of this decision, both for myself and for my sister? Overall, this is a complex situation with no easy answers. It involves balancing loyalty to a friend, support for a sibling, and maintaining personal boundaries. I need to weigh the pros and cons carefully and consider how my decision will impact everyone involved in the long run.
